item.title: Pope Leo XIV’s Post-Operative Update
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo V.
item.description:
A statement from the Holy See’s Press Office this afternoon detailed Pope Leo XIV’s post-operative progress. According to doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora, the Pope has resumed his daily activities and routine checks have been normal. A chest X-ray showed good recovery of the operated lung, and he completed full physical therapy sessions. Overall, his post-operative recovery is proceeding regularly. More: Messainlatino

item.title: Mexican Church holds colloquium on forgotten period of fierce persecution
item.dc:creator: David Ramos
item.description:
Bishop Héctor Mario Pérez Villarreal, secretary general of the Mexican Bishops’ Conference, encouraged participation in the colloquium ‘One Hundred Years Since the Start of the Cristero Resistance’ in Mexico City. The event, organized by the Mexican Bishops’ Conference and the Pontifical University of Mexico, aims to understand the history of the Cristiada, a conflict between Catholics and the Mexican state in the 1920s, and commemorate the faith witness of Mexicans. Pérez Villarreal emphasized that the conflict was about religious freedom, not violence, and that the colloquium seeks to delve into the truth and complete the understanding of this chapter in Mexican history. More: EWTN News

item.title: Bishop Wilmer Emphasizes the Role of Families in Faith Transmission
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
Bishop Heiner Wilmer, President of the German Bishops’ Conference, highlighted the importance of families in transmitting Christian faith at a Vatican meeting of bishops from around the world. The gathering, convened by Pope Leo XIV to mark the tenth anniversary of ‘Amoris laetitia,’ discussed challenges in marriage and family life. Wilmer noted that families, including grandparents and children, play crucial roles in faith education, citing examples like the ‘Sternsinger’ mission. The meeting also addressed controversial issues, such as the handling of divorced and remarried individuals and domestic violence, emphasizing the need for ongoing dialogue and pastoral care. More: Domradio

item.title: Pope Leo XIV as an Identifier for Suffering People
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV has become an identification figure for those suffering due to his open handling of his cancer, according to Vatican expert Marco Politi. This approach, also seen with Popes John Paul II and Francis, emphasizes that people with illnesses still possess dignity. Politi notes that Leo’s openness about his condition, especially after his lung surgery, has caused concern among many Italians. His communication style, influenced by his American background, contrasts with more traditional approaches, resonating with a diverse range of Catholic audiences in Europe and the US. More: Domradio

item.title: Cardinal Roche Speaks on Liturgical Issues in Exclusive Interview
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo V.
item.description:
Cardinal Arthur Roche, Prefect of the Dicastero per il culto divino e la disciplina dei sacramenti, discussed liturgical matters in an exclusive interview with AdVaticanum. He defended the post-Vatican II liturgy and criticized traditionalists, stating that they are moving away from the center of Catholicism. Roche, who has been in his role since 2021, emphasized the importance of unity in worship and the need to embrace changes introduced after the Council. He also addressed the use of pre-Vatican II liturgical books and the validity of the Priestly Fraternity of St. Pius X’s sacraments. More: Messainlatino

item.title: Congolese Theologian Denies African Polygamy as Moral Failure
item.dc:creator: INFOVATICANA
item.description:
Égide Muziazia, a Congolese priest and theologian from Münster, Germany, argues that African polygamy is a social institution rather than a moral failing. He criticizes missionary actions that imposed monogamy, leading to injustices. Muziazia praises a SECAM document supporting pastoral practices in African Churches, emphasizing the need for contextual understanding. He concludes that no continent can universalize its own response, advocating for a communion of contexts rather than uniformity. More: InfoVaticana

item.title: Building bridges between faith and education in Kazakhstan
item.dc:creator: Unknown
item.description:
St. Lawrence School in Kornewka, founded in 1996 by Fr. Lorenz Gawol, has grown to serve over 200 students from diverse religious backgrounds. The school, now led by Fr. Leopold Kropfreiter, promotes a Christian vision of the human person through education and ethics while fostering intercultural and interreligious relationships. The school offers special skills like language and digital literacy, preparing students for future opportunities. Despite challenges, the school continues to serve as a bridge between culture and faith, helping young people in Northern Kazakhstan discover their potential. More: Vatican News

item.title: Pope Leo XIV Spends Night Well After Lung Surgery at Gemelli Hospital
item.dc:creator: INFOVATICANA
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV is recovering well after undergoing surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung at the Gemelli Polyclinic in Rome. The operation, led by Professor Stefano Margaritora, was successful, and the Pope has resumed his daily activities. He concelebrated Mass in a specially set up chapel on the hospital’s tenth floor. This is the first hospitalization during Leo XIV’s pontificate, following a routine check-up that detected a pulmonary nodule at an early stage. More: InfoVaticana

item.title: Holy See Urges International Cooperation to Combat Transnational Crime
item.dc:creator: Unknown
item.description:
At the Fifth Meeting of National Authorities on Transnational Organised Crime in Washington, D.C., Archbishop Juan Antonio Cruz Serrano, Permanent Observer of the Holy See to the Organisation of American States, called for stronger international cooperation to protect human dignity and safeguard vulnerable populations. He emphasized placing the human person at the center of security strategies, strengthening international cooperation, and investing in prevention and protection, particularly for minors in the digital environment. Archbishop Cruz Serrano highlighted the need to combat illicit financial flows and warned about the exploitation of minors through digital technology. More: Vatican News

item.title: FSSPX Continues Legal Battle Against Excommunications in Rome
item.dc:creator: InfoVaticana
item.description:
The Priestly Fraternity of Saint Pius X (FSSPX) is pursuing legal avenues in Rome against excommunications declared by the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith following episcopal consecrations at Écône. The Fraternity’s General House has stated that it has followed the procedures provided by canon law and requests that the legal and doctrinal objections raised be examined. The matter is now before unspecified competent authorities, and the Fraternity will maintain discretion during the proceedings. The appeal continues amid strained relations between Rome and the traditionalist world, with Cardinal Arthur Roche stating that the Pope will not change Traditionis custodes or return to Summorum Pontificum. More: InfoVaticana
